## Your turn {#independent}

Simplify $\displaystyle\frac{(2ab^3)^2}{8a^3b}$ with positive indices. Show what happens to the coefficient, $a$ and $b$.

<details name="independent-working">
<summary>Reminder</summary>

Expand the numerator first. Use the numerator exponent minus the denominator exponent for each base.

</details>

<details name="independent-working">
<summary>Check my working</summary>

$\dfrac{4a^2b^6}{8a^3b}=\dfrac12 a^{2-3}b^{6-1}=\dfrac{b^5}{2a}$. Compare the exponent of each letter before moving the factor with a negative exponent.

</details>

<details name="independent-working">
<summary>Try a similar question</summary>

Simplify $\dfrac{(3pq^2)^2}{6p^4q}$.

</details>

<details name="independent-working">
<summary>Check the retry</summary>

$\dfrac{9p^2q^4}{6p^4q}=\dfrac32 p^{-2}q^3=\dfrac{3q^3}{2p^2}$.
